title: Easter Monday, 2025
hook: Francis dies on Easter Monday, the day after blessing the crowd at Easter

segments.voice: Yesterday, the empty square, and the monstrance he held up: Francis praying alone in the rain, the great square in front of him without a single pilgrim. Your line was we are in the same boat. Who turned out to be in the boat with you? Day nine hundred thirty-seven.

Easter Sunday in Rome, and the square that stood empty in yesterday's story is packed. Flags, umbrellas, phones held high. On the balcony of Saint Peter's, a frail man in a wheelchair is brought out, his voice thin after a long illness. He wishes the crowd a happy Easter, and someone beside him reads his Easter message aloud, because he can't. Then, instead of going back inside to rest, he rides down into the square in the open car, slowly, through the people, blessing children held up to him. The next morning, Easter Monday, Pope Francis died. Today is about that day, and about where it falls.
screen: `A FULL SQUARE ON EASTER SUNDAY.` → `A FRAIL BLESSING FROM THE BALCONY.` → `THE NEXT MORNING, HE DIES.`

segments.voice: For some families, Easter Monday is a leftover day. In Italy it even has a nickname, Pasquetta, little Easter, a day for picnics and the last of the chocolate. But in the Church's calendar, Easter Monday is not simply the day after Easter. It is still Easter. The Church's norms for the liturgical year say that the first eight days of the Easter season make up the octave of Easter, and each one is celebrated as a solemnity of the Lord. At Mass that Monday, the alleluias are still ringing, and the prayers still speak of this day, as if the sun hasn't set on the empty tomb. Easter, the calendar says in effect, is too large for a single sunrise. So when the news came, Catholics heard it inside that long day. A man who had just blessed the city and the world on Easter died while the Church was still singing about the resurrection. One of the Gospel readings the Church offers for funerals is Jesus speaking to Martha in John's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the resurrection and the life: he that believeth in me, although he be dead, shall live." The same promise is offered at the funeral of anyone who dies in the faith, famous or not. Francis seems to have wanted his own burial to look just as ordinary. He had asked to be buried simply, outside the Vatican, in the Roman basilica of Saint Mary Major, where he used to pray before and after his journeys, under a plain stone carrying only his name in Latin: Franciscus. For the world outside, Easter Monday is a holiday in some places and a workday in others. For the Church it is still Easter morning. Both were true that day, at the same time.
screen: `EASTER MONDAY IS STILL EASTER.` · `AN OCTAVE: EIGHT DAYS KEPT AS ONE.` · `A DEATH INSIDE THE EASTER SEASON.` · `A PLAIN STONE: FRANCISCUS.` · then, large: `I AM THE RESURRECTION AND THE LIFE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: remember the popes who have died. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind the popes you've met in these lessons, or the ones from your own lifetime. Francis. Benedict. John Paul. Whoever comes. Don't sum them up or grade them. Just say each name slowly, one at a time, and let it rest. The Church's old prayer for the dead asks God to grant them eternal rest and to let perpetual light shine on them. If you pray, you can say that prayer after each name. If you don't, give each name one quiet breath before the next. The bell holds the time.
Easter Monday. The day after Easter Sunday, which the Church's calendar still keeps as Easter, inside the octave. The day Pope Francis died.

Your line: the day after easter. Today, notice one thing still going after its big moment has passed: a kindness from yesterday, a song still in your head, a meal still feeding someone. Day nine hundred thirty-seven.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the eight days from Easter Sunday as the octave of Easter, celebrating each day at Mass as Easter itself, and when a pope dies they pray for him at Masses offered for the repose of his soul.

notes: Claims rule: the date (21 April 2025) and Francis's age are not spoken; the title keeps the index year.

Confirm: on Easter Sunday Francis appeared on the central loggia in a wheelchair, greeted the crowd, the Urbi et Orbi message was read by another prelate, and he then rode through the square in the popemobile blessing children.
Confirm: Francis's testament asked for burial in St Mary Major, in the ground, simple, with only the inscription 'Franciscus'; and that he prayed there before and after journeys.
Confirm GNLYC no. 24 wording: the first eight days of Easter Time are the octave, celebrated as solemnities of the Lord.
John 11:21-27 is among the Gospel options in the Order of Christian Funerals; confirm.
The prayer for the dead (eternal rest / perpetual light) is described, not quoted.
Editor: softened two sweeping 'a lot of families / a lot of people' claims about Easter Monday to 'some families' and 'a holiday in some places and a workday in others'.

Audit: 'not the day after Easter at all' (contradicted the carry) now 'not simply the day after Easter'; cut 'those words are read for popes... in exactly the same way', which implied John 11 was read at Francis's funeral (his funeral Gospel was John 21); now says the promise is offered at anyone's funeral.
